successors.note: Dutthagamani (Dutugemunu), Kavantissa's son, "reigned from 161 BC to 137 BC" and his victory at Anuradhapura "gave him rule over nearly the entire island" (Dutthagamani page); the anuradhapura dossier carries the matching gain in -161.

capitals.name: Magama (Mahagama, modern Tissamaharama)
capitals.note: The Ruhuna page names no capital but says Magama, Tissamaharama and Mahanagakula (now Ambalantota) were established in Ruhuna; the Dutthagamani page has a battle "near Mahagama". The coordinates are approximate (no page gives them).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Ruhuna row. The Ruhuna page gives the ancient extent as "mainly the Southern Province, a large part of Uva Province, and small parts of Sabaragamuwa and Eastern Provinces"; the Dutthagamani page has Kavantissa's border on the Mahaganga, "possibly the modern Menik Ganga", and his refusal to cross it ("the land on this side of the river is enough"). The six districts are the researcher's reading; the anuradhapura dossier hands over four of them (Hambantota, Monaragala, Matara, Ampara) in -161.

region.text: "the Southern Province, a large part of Uva Province, and small parts of Sabaragamuwa and Eastern Provinces" (the Ruhuna page); the Dutthagamani page: Kavantissa's "small southeast kingdom outside Rajarata's influence"

ledger.note: 205 BCE: Kavan Tissa reigns in Ruhuna, the southern kingdom Prince Mahanaga founded. The Kavan Tissa page gives his reign as 205-161 BC, ruling Ruhuna "at the same time as Kelani Tissa of Maya Rata"; the Ruhuna page: "Ruhuna was founded around 200 BC by Prince Mahanaga, brother to Devanampiya Tissa of Anuradhapura", after a personal dispute. The founding year is the earliest dated reign; the page's own founding date is about five years later.

region.text: "the Southern Province, a large part of Uva Province, and small parts of Sabaragamuwa and Eastern Provinces" (the Ruhuna page); the Dutthagamani page: Kavantissa's "small southeast kingdom outside Rajarata's influence"

ledger.note: 161 BCE: Dutugemunu, king of Ruhuna, takes Anuradhapura and unites the island. "from 161 BC to 137 BC" is his reign; "Victory at Anuradhapura gave him rule over nearly the entire island", and the page does not date the Battle of Vijithapura or Elara's death. Elara's invasion of Anuradhapura is dated 205 BC on the same page, which gives 44 years to 161.

region.text: "the Southern Province, a large part of Uva Province, and small parts of Sabaragamuwa and Eastern Provinces" (the Ruhuna page); the Dutthagamani page: Kavantissa's "small southeast kingdom outside Rajarata's influence"

ledger.note: 161 BCE: the kingdom of Ruhuna ends as a separate state when Kavantissa's son becomes king of the whole island. The page gives no date for Kavantissa's death or for the war with Dutugemunu's brother Tissa (battles at Culanganiyapitthi and near Mahagama) that preceded it. The Ruhuna page says Ruhuna "repeatedly rebelled against the superior states in Rajarata" later, without dates; that later history is not covered here.

wars.name: Dutugemunu's conquest of Rajarata
wars.outcome: Dutugemunu "subdued as many as 32 Tamil rulers" and killed Elara in single combat at the eastern gate of Anuradhapura after a four-month siege of Vijitanagara; he ruled nearly the entire island.
wars.note: The page gives no year for the siege, the single combat or Elara's death; -161 is the start of his reign over the island, and the campaign must have run before it. No zone is drawn because the land fought over (Rajarata and the north) belongs to the anuradhapura dossier's shape.

wars.name: Dutugemunu against his brother Tissa

zones.text: "the Southern Province, a large part of Uva Province, and small parts of Sabaragamuwa and Eastern Provinces" (the Ruhuna page); the Dutthagamani page: Kavantissa's "small southeast kingdom outside Rajarata's influence"

wars.outcome: After Kavantissa's death Dutugemunu lost the first battle at Culanganiyapitthi, won one near Mahagama and was reconciled with Tissa, who became a general.
wars.note: Both battles are undated on the page.

certainty.note: The only frontier named is the Mahaganga ("possibly the modern Menik Ganga") between Ruhuna and Rajarata; everything else is a province-level reading.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks (sa-02-a asked for it: years -205..-161 are the span the pages place it). Three pages opened (budget 2-5). The dossier ends in -161 because no page opened dates anything of Ruhuna after that. The Ruhuna page continues its history (rebellions against Rajarata, Vijayabahu I's defeat of Chola generals, Parakramabahu I's annexation) with no dates, and the anuradhapura dossier has Mahinda V fleeing to Ruhuna in 993: that later Ruhuna (c. 993-12th century) is a second period of independence that needs its own pages (sa-03, Polonnaruwa). The founding conflict: Ruhuna page "around 200 BC"; Kavan Tissa reign from 205. The traditional date of Mahanaga (brother of Devanampiya Tissa) is earlier than either and no page opened gives it. The extent is the page's province list; the anuradhapura dossier (-161 gain) uses four of the six districts. Gazetteer names needed: none (admin-1 units resolve), Magama/Tissamaharama and Mahaganga are text only.
